keywords_en: Criminal; Justifiable Defense; First Instance; Basic People's Court; Jilin Province; Natural Person; Criminal Law; Determination of Justifiable Defense; Boundary between Excessive Defense and Justifiable Defense; Support Plaintiff; Intentional Injury; Stabbing to Death with a Knife; Voluntary Surrender
full_text_en:
Zhu Xiaohong — case of justifiable defense

Defendant: Zhu Xiaohong, female, 29 years old, formerly a savings bank clerk at the Egg and Poultry Company of Changchun City, Jilin Province; arrested on November 9, 1993 for intentional injury.

The case of defendant Zhu Xiaohong's intentional injury was initiated by the Nanguan District People's Procuratorate of Changchun City, Jilin Province, which filed a public prosecution with the Nanguan District People's Court on January 25, 1994.

The Nanguan District People's Procuratorate charged that: At approximately 20:00 on September 9, 1993, defendant Zhu Xiaohong and her younger sister Zhu Xiaomei were carrying water home when they saw the victim Li Zhiwen fighting and grappling with Zhu Xiaohong's mother, Liu Zhenling. Upon seeing Zhu Xiaomei, Li Zhiwen kicked her to the ground and, holding a fruit knife, declared: "If you don't date me, I'll sever your foot tendons." Seeing this, Liu Zhenling struck Li Zhiwen on the head with a flashlight and told Zhu Xiaomei to run. Zhu Xiaomei took the opportunity to flee outside. At that moment, Li Zhiwen turned and slashed Liu Zhenling's left forearm three times with the fruit knife. Zhu Xiaohong stepped forward to stop him, and Li Zhiwen rushed at her, stabbing her right hand. Then, Liu Zhenling used the flashlight to knock the fruit knife from Li Zhiwen's hand. Zhu Xiaohong grabbed the knife first and stabbed Li Zhiwen several times in the chest and abdomen. Forensic examination determined that Li Zhiwen died from acute hemorrhagic shock caused by hemopneumothorax resulting from sharp force injuries to the right lung and liver. After the incident, Zhu Xiaohong surrendered herself. The procuratorate alleged that Zhu Xiaohong's conduct constituted excessive defense and the crime of intentional injury, and that she should be criminally punished according to law.

The Nanguan District People's Court, upon trial, found the following facts: The victim Li Zhiwen wanted to date Zhu Xiaomei, repeatedly pestered and blocked her, and after being rejected, threatened and intimidated her while waiting for an opportunity to retaliate. At approximately 20:00 on September 9, 1993, Li Zhiwen forcibly entered Zhu Xiaomei's home carrying a knife, and began quarreling and fighting with Zhu Xiaomei's mother, Liu Zhenling. Li Zhiwen declared: "I've come to settle accounts with you; today I'll sever Zhu Xiaomei's foot tendons." While they were fighting, Zhu Xiaomei entered the room. Upon seeing her, Li Zhiwen kicked her to the ground, held up the fruit knife, and shouted: "If you won't date me, I'll sever your foot tendons." He then thrust the knife at Zhu Xiaomei. Seeing this, Liu Zhenling struck Li Zhiwen on the head with a flashlight. Li Zhiwen turned back and fought with Liu Zhenling, allowing Zhu Xiaomei to escape out the door. At that point, defendant Zhu Xiaohong entered the room and, seeing Li Zhiwen thrusting the knife at her mother, stepped forward to stop him. Li Zhiwen then stabbed Zhu Xiaohong's right hand. Liu Zhenling used the flashlight to knock the fruit knife from Li Zhiwen's hand to the ground. Zhu Xiaohong grabbed the knife, and Li Zhiwen struggled with her to take it, fighting and grappling. During the struggle, Zhu Xiaohong stabbed Li Zhiwen multiple times in the chest and abdomen. Forensic examination determined that Li Zhiwen died from acute hemorrhagic shock caused by hemopneumothorax resulting from sharp force injuries to the right lung and liver. After the incident, Zhu Xiaohong surrendered to the public security authorities.

It was also found that the victim Li Zhiwen had previously been detained for hooliganism and molesting women, subjected to re-education through labor for fighting and brawling, sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment for theft, and was, before the incident, wanted by the public security authorities for theft.

The above facts are confirmed by witness testimony, forensic examination, and the record of crime scene inspection, and the defendant Zhu Xiaohong also made a confession. The evidence is reliable and sufficient.

The Nanguan District People's Court held that: The victim Li Zhiwen had previously been detained and subjected to re-education through labor for hooliganism, molesting women, and fighting and brawling; had been sentenced to imprisonment for theft; and was later wanted by the public security authorities for theft. During this period, Li Zhiwen used pestering and threats to compel Zhu Xiaomei to date him. After being rejected by Zhu Xiaomei, Li Zhiwen carried a knife and committed unlawful infringement against Zhu Xiaohong, Zhu Xiaomei, and Liu Zhenling. Defendant Zhu Xiaohong, when her own life and that of her mother Liu Zhenling were under serious threat, in order to stop the unlawful infringement, and while the unlawful infringement was in progress, stabbed Li Zhiwen with the knife, causing his death. The nature of her conduct lacked social harmfulness, constituted a defensive act, and the degree of defense was appropriate. Pursuant to the provision of Article 17, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, which states: "...an act of justifiable defense taken to protect the person or other rights of oneself or others from ongoing unlawful infringement shall not bear criminal liability," Zhu Xiaohong's conduct did not constitute a crime. Accordingly, on March 5, 1994, the Nanguan District People's Court rendered the following judgment: The defendant Zhu Xiaohong is acquitted.

After the first instance judgment was announced, the Nanguan District People's Procuratorate filed a protest with the Changchun Intermediate People's Court, on the grounds that the Nanguan District People's Court's determination of the nature of the case was incorrect, the factual basis and legal grounds were insufficient, and that defendant Zhu Xiaohong's conduct constituted the crime of intentional injury and amounted to excessive defense.

During the second instance of the case, the Changchun City People's Procuratorate considered that the protest by the Nanguan District People's Procuratorate was improper and, pursuant to the provision of Article 133, Paragraph 2 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, issued on May 6, 1994, a decision to withdraw the protest to the Changchun Intermediate People's Court. The first instance judgment became legally effective.
